must: **Speedup** S = T(1)/T(p); **efficiency** E = S/p; **cost** C = p·T(p). Cost-optimal when C ≈ T(1).
**Strong** scaling = fixed problem; **weak** scaling = problem grows with p.
Higher **computation-to-communication ratio** → better speedup and scalability.
Summation tree: speedup peaks around p = 128 then **falls** because communication (log p) grows while work (n/p) shrinks.
Distributed memory → **MPI**; shared memory → **Pthreads/OpenMP/CUDA**, risk of **race conditions**.
Design considerations: **partitioning (data/task/model), communication, synchronisation, load balancing**.
TOP500 = LINPACK (Ax = b) in FLOP/s; Green500 = FLOP/s **per watt**. HPC = MPI + OpenMP + CUDA.
formulas: S = T(1)/T(p)   E = S/p   C = p·T(p)
Summation model: T(p) = 7·log₂p + n/p − 1  (T(2)=518, T(4)=269, T(8)=148)
traps: Forgetting that cost grows even while speedup rises.
Quoting scalability without saying strong or weak.
Calling a race's result 'the last writer wins' — it's **unpredictable**.
likely: Given T(1), T(p): compute S, E, C and comment on cost-optimality.
Explain why speedup drops after a certain p.
Classify examples as data / task / model parallelism.
tricks: Design steps = **'PCSL'**: Partition, Communicate, Synchronise, Load-balance.
